title: Renewable Energy
seo_title: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Renewable Energy Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Science and Development
standard_text: Energy resources are renewable (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass) or non-renewable (coal, oil, natural gas); Nigeria uses hydroelectric and solar power; using energy wisely and sustainably. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: Science and Development)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Science and Development): renewable and non-renewable resources, solar, wind, hydro and geothermal power, and saving energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Nigeria gets most of its renewable electricity from hydroelectric dams.
body_html:
How to think about it

Non-renewable resources such as coal, oil and natural gas formed over millions of years and will run out; burning them releases carbon dioxide. Renewable resources such as sunlight, wind, flowing water, geothermal heat and biomass are replaced naturally.

Nigeria generates electricity from hydroelectric dams on the River Niger and River Kaduna (Kainji, Jebba and Shiroro), and more and more homes, schools and clinics use solar panels. Each source has advantages and disadvantages; saving energy at home also helps.

Example

Is coal renewable?

Formed over millions of years

Answer: no

Example

Which energy uses heat from inside the Earth?

Volcanic areas

Answer: geothermal energy

Common mistakes

  • Thinking renewable means it has no environmental effects.
  • Thinking solar panels work only at noon.
  • Mixing up hydro (water) and geothermal (underground heat).

faq.q: Why does Nigeria have hydroelectric power?
faq.a: Dams on large rivers such as the Niger turn the energy of flowing water into electricity.

faq.q: Why is wind power not always available?
faq.a: The wind does not blow at the same speed all the time.

items.q: Which is used to turn wind into electricity or motion?
items.e: Energy from wind is used with wind turbines.

items.q: People use wind turbines to get energy from wind. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It never affects the environment in any way.
It makes new energy from nothing.
They make no air pollution while working.
It works the same in every place on Earth.
items.e: They make no air pollution while working.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Oil formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: What does 'reduce, reuse, recycle' help save?
c: resources and the energy needed to make new things
items.e: Making new products uses energy.

items.q: A stretched elastic band stores which form of energy?
items.e: It is released when let go.

items.q: Which is used to turn heat inside Earth into electricity or motion?
c: a gas stove or gas power station
a dam with a power station
items.e: Energy from heat inside Earth is used with a geothermal power station.

items.q: Dayo reads about a resource that formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how coal formed.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?

items.q: Ada reads about a resource that formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago. Which resource is it?

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?

items.q: Nonso reads about a resource that formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers. Which resource is it?

items.q: What energy change happens in a solar panel?
items.e: Solar cells change light into electricity.

items.q: Tobi asks how iron ore formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
items.e: Iron ore formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Wind is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: People use wind turbines to get energy from wind. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
Burning petrol pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
items.e: Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.

items.q: People use solar panels to get energy from sunlight. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Burning petrol pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
items.e: Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.

items.q: Why are LED bulbs better than old incandescent bulbs?
c: They are brighter only because they are hot.
They give the same light using much less electricity.
items.e: Less energy is wasted as heat.

items.q: People use a geothermal power station to get energy from heat inside Earth. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It makes very little air pollution.
It never affects the environment in any way.
It makes new energy from nothing.
It works the same in every place on Earth.
items.e: It makes very little air pollution.

items.q: Nkechi asks how coal formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
items.e: Coal formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years.

items.q: What is geothermal energy?
c: heat from inside Earth used for heating or to generate electricity
energy from the Sun's heat on rocks
items.e: Iceland and New Zealand use a lot of it.

items.q: Which human impact are wildlife crossings over or under roads designed to reduce?

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: dams blocking salmon from swimming upstream?
items.e: Engineers design solutions that reduce harm to natural systems.

items.q: What is the difference between porosity and permeability?
c: permeability is the amount of water stored
porosity is how easily water flows
porosity is how much open space a rock has; permeability is how easily water flows through it
items.e: Clay is porous but not permeable.

items.q: What is the Murray–Darling Basin Plan?
c: a plan to drain the rivers
a plan to build a new river
a plan for mining in the basin
a plan to share water between farms, towns and the environment so the river system stays healthy
items.e: It sets sustainable diversion limits.

items.q: Which practice reduces soil erosion on farms?
c: keeping ground cover, such as stubble retention and no-till farming
items.e: Bare soil blows and washes away.

items.q: What happens if groundwater is pumped faster than it is recharged?
c: the water table falls and bores may run dry
items.e: This is groundwater mining.

items.q: What is sustainable yield?
c: the amount of a resource that can be taken without reducing its long-term availability

items.e: Used for fisheries, forests and water.

items.q: Which of these is a nonrenewable resource?
items.e: Nonrenewable resources form over millions of years or are not replaced at all.

items.q: Which human impact are wastewater treatment plants designed to reduce?
c: highways cutting animals off from their habitat

items.q: What is a disadvantage of solar and wind power?
c: their output varies with weather and time of day, so storage or backup is needed
items.e: Batteries and pumped hydro store energy.

items.q: What is an artesian aquifer?
c: a confined aquifer in which pressure pushes water up a bore without pumping
items.e: It is trapped between impermeable layers.

items.q: A landfill is filling up quickly. Which solution best addresses this problem?

items.q: An old bulb uses 75 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 11 watts. A school replaces 8 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (75 − 11) × 8 = 512 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power stations.
